title: Persona
description: Everything that makes the desk character a specific person. This file is the contract: hand it to an LLM together with your CV and it has enough to write a valid persona without seeing the source.

role.description: Your job title, as you would want it read aloud.

location.description: City and country, optionally with a work-mode note.

hair.description: 'long' adds hair falling past the shoulders.

script.description: The commands the character types, in order. Five to seven is the useful range: fewer and it reads as a gimmick, more and nobody sees the end. Give each one a different discipline.

prompt.description: The command, including the leading '$ '. It does not have to be a real command — it has to read like one. 22 characters is what fits on the screen.

lines.description: Output. In the default 'grid' layout these are laid out two per row, so 6 tokens fill the screen exactly. Anything beyond 6 renders behind the laptop bezel and is invisible.

layout.description: 'grid' pairs the lines into two columns and caps each at 10 characters. 'list' gives each its own full-width row, which fits 3 lines instead of 6 — use it for sentences.

hold.description: Milliseconds the completed frame stays on screen before clearing.
